prompt: A summarization service meets average quality goals but produces different omissions on repeated runs for the same long case file. Release approval currently uses one run per case. What is the strongest adjustment?

options.text: Increase the context window and assume repeatability improves as the full file fits.
Run the same prompt once more only when the first summary looks unusually short.

Evaluate repeated runs across representative long and short cases, track omission variance, and set a release threshold for the risky fields.

prompt: A natural-language triage assistant sometimes follows a reviewer’s requested format and sometimes adds an unrequested paragraph. The output must satisfy a strict downstream JSON schema. What should the architect do?

options.text: Use the model for interpretation, then validate the response against a schema and reject or repair invalid structure before downstream use.
Strengthen the prompt until formatting appears consistent, then pass responses directly to the parser.
Ask reviewers to manually remove extra paragraphs after the service has acted on the response.
Treat format adherence as a model-training issue and postpone release until a future model version.

feedback.reason: Steerability can improve formatting but is not a hard contract; a parser-facing schema needs deterministic validation and an explicit failure path.

prompt: A financial assistant must classify a request into one of four supported account actions. The model is broadly helpful but occasionally invents a fifth action that the ledger does not support. Which design best respects the model’s limits?

options.text: Ask for a longer chain of reasoning and let the assistant decide whether a fifth action is useful.
Use a larger context budget so all historical account activity is available before choosing.
Constrain the action field to the four supported values and have the application reject any value outside the ledger contract.
Tell the model that it is highly steerable and should never produce unsupported actions.

feedback.reason: The ledger contract is an explicit finite rule, so the application must enforce the allowed action set even if prompting lowers violations.

details.mechanismOrProperty: Steerability is useful but not equivalent to deterministic enforcement; the finite domain belongs in code or schema validation.

details.boundaryOrTradeoff: A valid action enum still requires authorization and business-rule checks before a consequential ledger update.

details.transfer: Map each model property to a corresponding architectural control and keep application invariants outside the model.
